verdict.rationale: ROS 2 has no API-credential system for AI agents. It does offer SROS2/DDS-Security: you create a keystore, and each security enclave carries a single communication policy that authenticates participants and controls communications across the graph. An agent running as a ROS node could therefore get a scoped identity, which partially matches the least-privilege intent. Missing for 10: agent-oriented API credential issuance, documented per-topic/service permission granularity in the evidence, credential rotation/revocation details, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
